## 10-Week Exam Prep Method Comparison

Method **B** is more effective for exam performance because **active recall + spaced repetition** produces stronger long-term retention than passive rereading.
Given the time limit, the student should **not** try to copy either method exactly; instead, compress Method B into the available study time.

## Best Fit for the Available Schedule

| Method | Effectiveness | Fit for 1h weekdays / 3h weekends | Main Strength | Main Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: 2h passive rereading daily | Low to moderate | Poor | Easy to start, low effort | Weak retention, inefficient use of time |
| B: 90m active recall + spaced repetition daily | High | Good, with adjustment | Better memory, better exam transfer | Needs structure and discipline |
| Recommended: compressed Method B | Highest | Best fit | Maximizes learning per minute | Requires planning and review system |

## Adapted Plan for the Time Limit

### Weekdays: 60 minutes
- **10 min**: quick review of yesterday’s mistakes or flashcards
- **35 min**: active recall on one topic set
- **15 min**: spaced repetition of older material

### Weekends: 3 hours
- **45 min**: mixed active recall on all prior topics
- **60 min**: timed practice questions or past paper section
- **30 min**: review errors and make correction notes
- **45 min**: spaced repetition of weak areas

### 10-Week Structure
- **Weeks 1-3**: build core notes into questions, flashcards, and short recall prompts
- **Weeks 4-6**: increase retrieval practice and add timed questions
- **Weeks 7-8**: focus on weak topics and mixed-topic recall
- **Weeks 9-10**: full review, past papers, and error correction

## Practical Recommendation

- Use **Method B as the base**
- Replace long rereading with:
  - self-quizzing
  - flashcards
  - closed-book summaries
  - past-paper questions
- Keep rereading only as a **brief support tool** when a topic is first introduced or when correcting mistakes
